# the contributor audit of the final selector obstruction

This is an independent audit of
`candidate e13ef2bc2dcc3baf`, not an affirmative
proof or a counterexample to OC.

## Actual fibers and measure

The midpoint simplex has apex `(0,11/12,0,0,0)` and base at
`x_1=497/3000`; the four base edge vectors have length `3979/6000` in
four distinct coordinate directions. Its relative five-volume is therefore
exactly `r T^4`. The two exact rational comparisons imply
`0<2-q<2/11`, `q<2`, and `0<a<10^-5`. All three fibers have positive
five-volume. Convexity and `(A+C)/2=D subset B` show that taking their
ambient convex hull adds no points to the middle fiber outside B. There
are no integer base indices other than -1, 0, and 1.

## Every proposed selector is covered

The centroid of every dominated submeasure of C is in C. Its midpoint
with the centroid of A is a convex combination of two points of D.
Consequently the entire proposed free-mixture candidate set is contained
in `conv(g_B,D)`, including arbitrary fractional selections. The wedge
inequality `R x_1+x_2 >= (R+1)/6` holds throughout D. If a point of this
larger hull misses the first closed cap, it belongs strictly to the
second one because `R alpha=9/25>17/50=beta`. Equality on the first cap
boundary is covered by its closedness.

## Both cap masses and all endpoint points

The integer tilt of the first cap makes the maximum endpoint value
exactly r at BOTH endpoints, below its threshold. Its only mass is the
standard-simplex cap `(1-h_1)^5`. The second cap contains A in full and
excludes C in full, so its mass is `(1-h_2)^5+a`. The stated exact
mean-value and polynomial inequalities make both masses strictly less
than `gamma_5(1+a/2)`; the Fraction verifier was run independently by the
root and passes. There is no numerical fifth-root estimate in this step.

Every point of either endpoint simplex has an own-fiber vertex cap of
mass at most `gamma_5` times that fiber's mass. Because its integer index
is extreme, an arbitrarily large finite integer tilt isolates this cap
from both other compact fibers. This gives strict subtarget bounds for
all endpoint points.

## Scope

The failed center rules comprise the fixed-mixture selector, the entire
free-mixture selector, and all endpoint points. Middle points outside
`conv(g_B,D)` are not covered by this certificate. In particular the
example neither refutes OC nor supplies its missing general center.

the contributor verdict: PASS, with the preceding strict scope. Both other
independent mathematical agents also report PASS.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
